To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
both RNA binding domains (1-92 and (93-184) in A1 contribute to single-stranded-RNAs binding.

the two RBD domains in A1 contribute toward the binding of single-stranded-RNAs, that the binding of A1 to ssRNA is a relatively weak interaction, that A1 binding to poly(r(A)) is biphasic at low pH, and that the glycine-rich COOHT domain of A1 is an important determinant of binding affinity.

the two tandemly arranged RBDs of hnRNP-A1 contribute toward single stranded RNA binding and that the COOH-terminal domain of A1 contributes toward single-stranded RNA binding and may provide a regulatory mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the nucleic acid interaction determinants of the hnRNP A/B family of proteins and the elucidation of how they function in RNA metabolism.
the molecular mechanisms by which the A1 hnRNP recognizes and binds to ssRNA.

the identification of the structural features that contribute to the nucleic acid-binding properties of A1, a protein that has been shown to be involved in the regulation of alternative RNA splicing and that is a target for the HIV-1 Tat protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two tandem RNA binding domains in hnRNP A(1) contribute toward single-strand RNA binding, but do not account for the full binding affinity of the intact protein.
both RBDs contribute to the binding of A1 to RNA and that the COOH-terminal region of A1 is an important determinant of its affinity.
the two RBD domains of A1 are both necessary and sufficient to mediate ssRNA binding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both the 1-92 RBD and the 93-194 RBD of A1 contribute toward ssRNA binding.
both the 1-92 RBD and the 93-84 RBD contribute toward the single-stranded-RN-binding activity of A1.

the two RBD domains of A1 contribute to the binding of ssRNA, that both contribute equally to the binding of poly[r(epsilonA)], but that the 93- 184 domain contributes more than the 1-92 domain to A1 binding of ssRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although the individual RBD's of A1 bind ssRNA with relatively low affinity (1.5-4.5 x10(4)M-1) and a site size of 4 nucleotiles or less, they do contribute to the overall binding of A1 to ssRNA.
the two RBD-containing domains in hnRNP A(1) contribute equally to the binding of ssRNA.
the tandem arrangement of RBDs in hnRNPs may be a mechanism to increase the binding affinity for ssRNA targets.
